literal translation: Yes! I'm Shinobu, the happy-humming gal! Now, it's a chance! This round, points double, so do your best!
final English: Hi-hi! It's Shinobu, the happy-go-lucky gal! Here's your chance! Points are doubled this round, so go for it!

original Japanese:
いまの　かんじ　すっごくいいわ！
じゃあ　また　あなたのバイブが
あがってきたら　おあいしましょっ！
literal translation: That feeling just now was really good! Well, let's meet again when your vibes rise again!
final English: Ooh, that was super! Let's meet again when your vibes climb higher!

original Japanese:
うーん………　ちょっとものたりなかったわね！
でも　めげないでっ！　また　そのうち
あえると　おもうから　そのときは　………ヨ！
literal translation: Hmm... that was a little unsatisfying! But don't get discouraged! I think we'll meet again sometime, so at that time... (you know)!
final English: Hmm… that wasn't quite enough! But don't let it get you down! I bet we'll meet again someday, and next time, I'm counting on you!

original Japanese:
はいっ！　きゃぴきゃぴギャルの　しのぶよっ！
ぱんぱかぱーん！　なんと　すてきなあなたに
ボーナス　{V}{V}{V}{V}てん　どーんとしんていよっ！
literal translation: Yes! I'm Shinobu, the bubbly gal! Ta-da! To wonderful you, I'm boldly presenting a bonus of {V}{V}{V}{V} points!
final English: Hi-hi! It's Shinobu, the bubbly gal! Ta-daaa! A whopping bonus of {V}{V}{V}{V} points, just for wonderful you!

original Japanese: {V}かいで　できないと　サイポイントがさがります
literal translation: If you can't do it in {V} times, Psi Points go down.
final English: {V} misses cost you points

original Japanese: ねんりきで　あのひとを　ふりむかせてください
literal translation: Please make that person turn around with psychokinesis.
final English: Turn that person around with Psychokinesis.

original Japanese: つぎにとおる　くるまのいろを　よちしてください
literal translation: Please foresee the color of the car that passes next.
final English: Please predict the color of the next car.

original Japanese: つぎに　ひとがでてくるばしょを　よちしてください
literal translation: Please foresee the place where a person comes out next.
final English: Please predict where the next person will appear.

original Japanese: ねんりきで　ふりむかせてください
literal translation: Please make (them) turn around with psychokinesis.
final English: Make them turn around with Psychokinesis.

original Japanese:
わたしは　ジエリコ　です。
{NAME}さんの　サイパワーを　ためしましょう。
よろしいですね。
literal translation: I am Jericho. Let us test {NAME}'s Psi Power. Is that all right?
final English: I am Jericho. Allow me to test your Psi Power, {NAME}. Shall we begin?

original Japanese:
また　おあいしましたね。
ちょうしは　いかがですか。
では　あなたの　サイパワーを　ためしましょう。
literal translation: We meet again. How is your condition? Then, let us test your Psi Power.
final English: We meet again. How are you today? Now, let us test your Psi Power.

original Japanese:
ここは　サイサロンです
スクールをそつぎょうした　エスパーのたまりばです
literal translation: This is the Psi Salon. It's a hangout for Espers who graduated from the School.
final English: This is Psi Salon, a hangout for Psychic School graduates.

original Japanese:
ここは　サイパークです
シテイーの　いこいのばしょです
literal translation: This is the Psi Park. It's the City's place of relaxation.
final English: This is Psi Park, where the City comes to relax.

original Japanese: なにも　かんじないぞ！
literal translation: I don't feel anything!
final English: I don't feel a thing!

original Japanese:
ぼくは　エスパーありまです
もしかしたら　きみは{NAME}さんじゃないの？

やっぱりね！
じつは　エスパーキヨタから　{NAME}さんのことはよくきいているよ。　かなり　そしつがあるってね
ところで　{NAME}さんの　めいしがわりに
スプーンをまげてみせてよ？
literal translation: I'm Esper Arima. Could it be you're {NAME}? (pause) I knew it! Actually, I've heard a lot about {NAME} from Esper Kiyota. That you have quite a lot of talent. By the way, {NAME}, in place of a business card, bend a spoon for me?
final English: I'm Esper Arima. Could you be {NAME}, by any chance?{P}I knew it! Esper Kiyota has told me a lot about you, {NAME}. He says you have real talent. Say, {NAME}, bend me a spoon as a business card?

original Japanese:
すごいね！
つよいバイブレーションをかんじたよ
literal translation: Amazing! I felt strong vibrations!
final English: Amazing! I felt some strong vibrations!

original Japanese: きょうは　ちょうしがわるいみたいだね
literal translation: Seems you're in bad condition today.
final English: Looks like you're off your game today.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さん　ずいぶんちょうしがいいみたいだね
また　みんなに　スプーンまげをみせてあげてよ
literal translation: {NAME}, you seem to be in very good condition. Show everyone spoon bending again.
final English: You're on a roll, {NAME}! Show everyone your spoon bending again!

original Japanese:
{NAME}さん　ずいぶんちょうしがいいみたいだね
こんどは　スプーンねじりをやってみせてよ
literal translation: {NAME}, you seem to be in very good condition. This time, show me spoon twisting.
final English: You're on a roll, {NAME}! Show me some spoon twisting this time!

original Japanese:
{NAME}さん　ずいぶんちょうしがいいみたいだね
こんどは　スプーンおりをやってみせてよ
literal translation: {NAME}, you seem to be in very good condition. This time, show me spoon breaking.
final English: You're on a roll, {NAME}! Show me some spoon snapping this time!

original Japanese: シンセサイザーがあるぞ！
literal translation: There's a synthesizer!
final English: There's a synthesizer!

original Japanese: なにか　おきものがあるぞ！
literal translation: There's some kind of ornament!
final English: There's some kind of figurine!

original Japanese:
ガムのはんばいきがあるぞ！
ひとつ　かってみよう
literal translation: There's a gum vending machine! Let's try buying one.
final English: There's a gum machine! Let's get a piece.

original Japanese:
わたしはマミよ
よろしくね
きょねん　サイキックスクールを　そつぎょうしたのあら！　{NAME}さんも　そつぎょうせいなの
じゃあ　わたしがせんぱいってわけね
このパークって　わたしとてもすきなのよね
サイのトレーニングで　よくやるんだけど
ねんりきで　あそこのふんすいって　だせるのよね
{NAME}さんも　いちどためしてみない
literal translation: I'm Mami. Nice to meet you. I graduated from Psychic School last year. Oh! {NAME}, you're a graduate too? Then I'm your senior. I really like this park. I often do it in psi training: with psychokinesis you can make that fountain over there spout. {NAME}, won't you try it once too?
final English: I'm Mami, nice to meet you! I finished Psychic School last year.{P}Oh, you're a graduate too, {NAME}? That makes me your senior!{P}I love this park. I train here a lot. Did you know you can make that fountain spout with Psychokinesis? Want to try, {NAME}?

original Japanese:
さすがね！
とてもつよい　サイパワーをかんじたわ
literal translation: As expected! I felt very strong Psi Power!
final English: Impressive! I felt very strong Psi Power!

original Japanese: ちょうしがあがったら　またやってみるといいわ
literal translation: When your condition goes up, it'd be good to try again.
final English: Give it another try when you're in better form.

original Japanese:
きょうの　バイブレーションは　いいみたいね
わたし　ふんすいがみたいな
literal translation: Today's vibrations seem good. I want to see the fountain.
final English: Your vibrations seem good today. I'd love to see the fountain spout!

original Japanese:
きょうは　わたしがふんすいを　だしてみるわ
{NAME}さんは　でるばしょを　よちしてみせてね
literal translation: Today I'll try making the fountain spout. {NAME}, show me you can foresee where it comes out.
final English: Today I'll make the fountain spout! {NAME}, predict where it shoots!

original Japanese:
あら{NAME}さん　ちょうどよかったわ
ふんすいが　こしょうしちゃったみたいなの
とうしをつかって　わるいところをさがしてくれない
literal translation: Oh, {NAME}, just in time. The fountain seems to have broken. Won't you use clairvoyance to find the bad spot?
final English: Oh, {NAME}, perfect timing! The fountain seems to be broken. Could you use Clairvoyance to find what's wrong?

original Japanese: {NAME}さんの　サイパワーを　みせてください
literal translation: Please show me {NAME}'s Psi Power.
final English: Please show me your Psi Power, {NAME}.

original Japanese: かだんがあるぞ！
literal translation: There's a flower bed!
final English: There's a flower bed!

original Japanese: ひこうせんの　かくのうこがあるぞ！
literal translation: There's an airship hangar!
final English: There's a blimp hangar!

original Japanese: さっき　バイブレーションをあわせたばしょだ
literal translation: It's the place where I tuned my vibrations a while ago.
final English: I tuned my vibrations here earlier.

original Japanese: じゅうじボタンで　いどうさきを　えらんでください
literal translation: Please choose a destination with the Control Pad.
final English: Please choose a destination with the Control Pad.

original Japanese: サイサロンへ　いどうちゅう
literal translation: Moving to the Psi Salon
final English: Heading to Psi Salon…

original Japanese: サイパークへ　いどうちゅう
literal translation: Moving to the Psi Park
final English: Heading to Psi Park…

original Japanese: サイランドへ　いどうちゅう
literal translation: Moving to Psi Land
final English: Heading to Psi Land…

original Japanese: テレポートちゅう！
literal translation: Teleporting!
final English: Teleporting!

original Japanese: スクールへ　いどうちゅう
literal translation: Moving to the School
final English: Heading to the School…

original Japanese:
ここはサイキックシテイーです。
あなたは　ここで　ちょうのうりょくの
じっせん　トレーニングを　つむことになります。
じぶんが　じっさいに　このせかいのなかに
あたかも　はいりこんだかのように　イメージして
トレーニングを　つむことが　たいせつです。
あせらず　ゆったりしたきもちで　やりましょう。
いままでと　おなじように　なにかをかんじたら
フイールコマンドを　つかってみてください。
literal translation: This is Psychic City. Here you will accumulate practical training in psychic powers. It's important to train while imagining as if you had actually entered this world yourself. Don't rush, do it with a relaxed feeling. Just as before, when you feel something, please try using the FEEL command.
final English: This is Psychic City. Here you will get hands-on training with your psychic powers. As you train, it is important to picture yourself truly inside this world. Take your time and stay relaxed. Just as before, when you sense something, try using the FEEL command.

original Japanese:
イベントに　せいこうすれば　ポイントが
あがります。　また　ポイントが　いってい
いじょうに　なると　サイレベルが　あがります。
レベルが　あがれば　キヨタから
ちょうのうりょくにかんする　じょうほうを
あなたは　きくことが　できるでしょう。
そして　レベルが　さいだいち　まで
あげることが　できたならば　いよいよ
さいしゅうイベントに　ちょうせんです。
literal translation: If you succeed at events, points go up. Also, when points exceed a certain amount, your Psi Level goes up. When your level goes up, you'll be able to hear information about psychic powers from Kiyota. And if you can raise your level to the maximum, at last you will challenge the final event.
final English: Succeed at events to earn points. Once your points pass a certain amount, your Psi Level goes up. As your level rises, Kiyota will tell you more about psychic powers. And once your level reaches its maximum, you can at last take on the final event.

original Japanese:
さいしゅうイベントに　せいこうしたならば
{NAME}さんは　エンデイングを　たいけんし
しんの　エスパーと　なることでしょう！
いまひかっている　ここが　センターです。
いどうするには　じゅうじボタンを　つかって
いどうさきを　えらび　Ａボタンをおします。
literal translation: If you succeed at the final event, {NAME} will experience the ending and become a true Esper! The place lit up now is the Center. To move, use the Control Pad to choose a destination and press the A Button.
final English: Succeed at the final event, {NAME}, and you will reach the ending as a true Esper! The glowing spot is the Center. To travel, choose a destination with the Control Pad and press the A Button.

original Japanese:
スプーンは　どこにでもあるから　いつでも
ねんりきの　トレーニングができるから　いいよね。さいしょは　なるべく　やわらかいスプーン　を
つかったほうが　いいみたいだね。
スプーンが　まがったときの　イメージをすると
やりやすいよね。
literal translation: Spoons are everywhere, so it's nice that you can do psychokinesis training anytime. At first it seems better to use spoons as soft as possible. It's easier if you picture the spoon when it has bent.
final English: Spoons are everywhere, so you can practice Psychokinesis any time. Nice, huh? Start with the softest spoons you can find. It helps to picture the spoon already bent.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんは　キヨタの　スプーンまげを
みたことって　ある？　あれは　すごいよね。
ぼくたちとは　バイブレーションが　ちがうよね。
literal translation: {NAME}, have you ever seen Kiyota's spoon bending? That's amazing. His vibrations are different from ours.
final English: {NAME}, have you ever seen Kiyota bend a spoon? It's amazing! His vibrations are on a whole other level from ours.

original Japanese:
フアミコンを　やっているときって
いしきの　レベルは　けっこう　いいらしいよ！
じつは　エスパーキヨタも　ゲームがすきなんだ。
ここだけの　はなしだけどさ
エスパーキヨタの　おやゆびには　たこ　があるんだフアミスタ　の　やりすぎだって　うわさだよ。
literal translation: When you're playing the Famicom, your level of consciousness is apparently pretty good! Actually, Esper Kiyota likes games too. Just between us, Esper Kiyota has a callus on his thumb. Rumor says it's from too much Famista.
final English: Playing the NES puts your mind in a pretty good state! Esper Kiyota loves games too. Just between us, he's got a callus on his thumb. Rumor says it's from too much R.B.I. Baseball!

original Japanese:
みのまわりにある　なにか　ひとつのものを　じっとみつづけると　いつもとは　ちがった　せかいを
かんじることが　できるように　なるよ。
literal translation: If you keep staring at one thing around you, you become able to sense a world different from usual.
final English: Pick one thing near you and keep staring at it. After a while, you'll start to sense a world different from your own.

original Japanese:
デジャブ　の　ことを　しっているかい？
はじめてきた　ばしょなのに　まえに　いちど
きたことが　あるように　かんじたことってない？
それを　デジャブ　と　いうんだよね。
あるしゅの　よち　のうりょく　とも　いえるね。
literal translation: Do you know about deja vu? Haven't you ever felt like you'd come to a place once before, even though it's your first time there? That's called deja vu. You could also call it a kind of precognitive ability.
final English: Know what déjà vu is? Have you ever visited a new place, yet felt like you've been there before? That's déjà vu, a kind of Precognition.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんは　ゆうれい　は　なんだとおもう？
ぼくは　あるしゅの　いしきエネルギーたい　だと
おもっているんだ。
literal translation: {NAME}, what do you think ghosts are? I think they're a kind of consciousness-energy body.
final English: {NAME}, what do you think ghosts are?{P}I think they're beings of conscious energy.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんは　じぶんが　うまれてくる　まえの
じょうたいを　かんじたことって　あるかな？
たぶん　ひかり　のイメージに　ちかいと　おもうな
literal translation: {NAME}, have you ever sensed your state before you were born? I think it's probably close to an image of light.
final English: {NAME}, have you ever sensed what it was like before you were born? I bet it's something close to light.

original Japanese:
さいきん　からだを　きたえているんだ。
こころと　からだの　バランスが　だいじだからね。{NAME}さんも　きたえた　ほうが　いいよ！
literal translation: I've been training my body lately. Because the balance of mind and body is important. You should train too, {NAME}!
final English: I've been working out lately. Mind and body need balance, you know. You should work out too, {NAME}!

original Japanese:
にんげんは　しんだら　どうなると　おもう？
し　とは　おわりではなく　つぎの　じげんでの
いしきの　しんか　を　いみしてるんじゃないかな
literal translation: What do you think happens to people when they die? Isn't death not an end, but the evolution of consciousness in the next dimension?
final English: What happens when we die? Maybe death isn't an end, but consciousness evolving to the next dimension.

original Japanese:
うちゅうは　ひとつだけじゃ　ないらしいね。
いくつかの　うちゅうが　どうじに　そんざい
してるみたいだね。
literal translation: Apparently the universe isn't just one. It seems several universes exist at the same time.
final English: I hear there isn't just one universe. Seems several of them exist side by side, all at once.

original Japanese:
{NAME}も　そろそろ　サイマスター　に　なれる
レベルに　なったね！
もう　ぼくも　かなわないよ。
literal translation: {NAME}, you've reached the level where you can soon become a Psi Master! I'm no match for you anymore.
final English: {NAME}, you're almost at Psi Master level! I'm no match for you anymore.

original Japanese:
おんなのこが　テレパシーで　かたりかけてきた
しかし　{NAME}の　レベルでは　ビジョンを
うけとることが　できないぞ！
literal translation: A girl spoke to you by telepathy. However, at {NAME}'s level, you can't receive the vision!
final English: A girl is reaching out by telepathy!{P}But {NAME}'s level is too low to receive her vision!

original Japanese:
ちょうのうりょくが　つかいこなせるようになると
いままで　かんじることの　できなかった　ちがったせかいを　みることが　できるわよ！
literal translation: Once you can master psychic power, you can see a different world you couldn't sense until now!
final English: Once you master your psychic powers, you'll see a whole new world you could never sense before!

original Japanese:
しぜんのもつ　バイブレーションって　いいわよね
いしや　きに　いしきを　あわせると　いろいろな
バイブを　かんじることが　できるわよ！
literal translation: Nature's vibrations are nice, aren't they? If you tune your consciousness to stones and trees, you can feel all kinds of vibes!
final English: Nature has such lovely vibrations! Tune your mind to stones and trees, and you can feel all kinds of vibes!

original Japanese:
ちょうのうりょくには　あい　の　パワーが　ひつようなの！　じぶんを　あいし　にんげんを　あいし
そして　うちゅうを　あいすることが　だいじだわ。
literal translation: Psychic power needs the power of love! Loving yourself, loving people, and loving the universe is what matters.
final English: Psychic power needs the power of love! Love yourself, love people, and love the universe. That's what matters.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんて　ゆめを　よくみるほうかな？
にんげんは　ねないと　いきては　いけないでしょ。だから　ゆめを　みるのも　ひつようよ。
ゆめ　の　せかいでは　みんなが　エスパーよ。
literal translation: {NAME}, are you someone who dreams a lot? People can't live without sleeping, right? So dreaming is necessary too. In the world of dreams, everyone is an Esper.
final English: {NAME}, do you dream a lot? People can't live without sleep, right? So we need our dreams too. In the world of dreams, everyone is an Esper.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんが　め　でみている　せかいは　ほんとうのせかいの　いちぶにしか　すぎないのよ。
でも　このせかいには　すべてが　あるの。おわかり
literal translation: The world you see with your eyes, {NAME}, is no more than a part of the real world. But in this world there is everything. Do you understand?
final English: The world you see with your eyes, {NAME}, is only a small part of reality. Yet this world holds everything. Do you see?

original Japanese:
わたしは　ほし　を　みるのが　すきなんだ。
ほし　を　みていると　じぶんは　うちゅうの
いちぶ　なんだなって　かんじるのよね！
literal translation: I like looking at the stars. When I look at the stars, I feel that I'm a part of the universe!
final English: I love stargazing. It makes me feel like part of the universe!

original Japanese:
テレポーテーションは　むずかしいわね。
いしきを　しゅうちゅう　しないと　なかなか
できないわ。　{NAME}さんは　もうできる？
literal translation: Teleportation is hard, isn't it? You can hardly do it unless you concentrate your consciousness. {NAME}, can you do it already?
final English: Teleportation is hard, isn't it? It's nearly impossible unless you really focus your mind. Can you do it yet, {NAME}?

original Japanese: このまちの　どこかに　パワースポットが　あるわ。そこには　テレポートで　いかなければ　ならないの{NAME}さんの　レベルでは　まだむりだわ！
literal translation: Somewhere in this town there is a Power Spot. You have to go there by teleport. At {NAME}'s level it's still impossible!
final English: Somewhere in this city there's a Power Spot. You must teleport there. You're not at that level yet, {NAME}!

original Japanese:
ずいぶん　サイレベルが　あがったわね！
もうちょっとで　パワースポットに　いけるわ。
あと　ちょっと　だから　がんばってね！
literal translation: Your Psi Level has gone up a lot! A little more and you can go to the Power Spot. Just a little more, so do your best!
final English: Your Psi Level has shot up! You're almost able to reach the Power Spot. Just a little more, so hang in there!

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんの　レベルなら　もう　テレポートが
できるはずよ。
パワースポット　には　いってみた？
literal translation: At {NAME}'s level, you should be able to teleport already. Have you tried going to the Power Spot?
final English: At your level, {NAME}, you should be able to teleport by now. Have you been to the Power Spot yet?

original Japanese: あなたって　ふかい　バイブレーションの　もちぬしね。　なんだか　かんじるものが　あるわ！
literal translation: You're the owner of deep vibrations. Somehow I feel something!
final English: Your vibrations run so deep. I can really feel something from you!

original Japanese: ちょうのうりょくは　だれにでもある　のうりょくなのに　なんで　みんなは　それに　きづかないのかしら？　ふしぎよね。
literal translation: Psychic power is an ability everyone has, so why doesn't everyone notice it? It's strange, isn't it?
final English: Everyone has ESP, so why doesn't anybody notice? Isn't that strange?

original Japanese:
あなたの　オーラ　とっても　きれいだわ！
でも　まだ　わたしほどじゃ　ないけどね………
literal translation: Your aura is very beautiful! But it's still not as much as mine…
final English: Your aura is so lovely! Not quite as lovely as mine, though…

original Japanese:
ねえ　ねえ　テレパシーで　なんか　ビジョンを
おくってみてよ！
literal translation: Hey, hey, try sending me some vision by telepathy!
final English: Hey, hey! Send me a vision by telepathy!

original Japanese:
あなたの　かんがえている　ビジョンが
わかるように　なってきたわ！
でも　あまり　へんな　ビジョンは　おくらないでね
literal translation: I've started to understand the visions you're thinking of! But don't send me too-strange visions, okay?
final English: I'm starting to pick up the visions you're thinking of! But don't send me anything too weird, okay?

original Japanese:
わたしの　こいびとを　おしえましょうか？
わたしを　おおきな　あいで　つつんでくれるの。
かれのことを　にんげんは　うちゅう　といってるわ
literal translation: Shall I tell you about my lover? He wraps me in great love. Humans call him 'the universe.'
final English: Shall I tell you who my sweetheart is? He wraps me in a great big love. Humans call him the universe.

original Japanese:
こんど　いっしょに　マインドトリップ
しましょうよ。
いしき　の　なかで　セッション　してみない。
literal translation: Let's do a Mind Trip together sometime. Won't you try a session inside consciousness?
final English: Let's Mind Trip together sometime. Care for a session, mind to mind?

original Japanese:
ちょうのうりょくを　わるいことに　つかったら
だめよ！　もっとも　あなたは　そんなことを
するような　ひとじゃ　ないものね。
literal translation: You mustn't use psychic power for bad things! Though you're not the kind of person who'd do that anyway.
final English: You mustn't use psychic powers for anything bad!{P}Not that you're the type to do that, of course.

original Japanese: あなた　さいきん　きれいな　め　になってきたね。め　をみると　そのひとの　こころが　わかるものなの。　わたしの　め　をじっと　みつめてみて。
literal translation: Your eyes have become beautiful lately. Looking at someone's eyes, you can understand their heart. Try gazing steadily into my eyes.
final English: Your eyes have grown so beautiful lately. The eyes show you a person's heart, you know. Gaze deep into mine.

original Japanese: こんど　ゆめ　のなかで　あいましょうよ。
literal translation: Let's meet in a dream sometime.
final English: Let's meet in a dream sometime.

original Japanese: ついに　あなたも　サイマスターね！
literal translation: At last, you too are a Psi Master!
final English: You're finally a Psi Master!

original Japanese: あそこにある　うごいている　おきものを　フイールしてみた？
literal translation: Have you tried to FEEL the moving ornament over there?
final English: Have you tried to FEEL that moving figurine over there?

original Japanese:
だれかに　サイパワーを　みせてと　たのまれたら
やってみせるのが　このシテイーでの　エチケットよ
literal translation: If someone asks you to show them your Psi Power, showing them is the etiquette in this City.
final English: In this City, if asked to show your Psi Power, it's polite to do so.

original Japanese: あなたの　スプーンまげって　きれ　が　あるわね！
literal translation: Your spoon bending has sharpness!
final English: Your spoon bending is so sharp!

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんは　スプーンを　ねじれるように
なったそうね。
literal translation: I hear {NAME} became able to twist spoons.
final English: I hear you can twist spoons now, {NAME}.

original Japanese:
いつか　どこかで　あなたに　あったような
き　がするわ！
literal translation: I feel like I've met you somewhere sometime!
final English: I feel like we've met before, somewhere, sometime!

original Japanese:
あそこにある　ガムのはんばいきを　フイール
してみた？
literal translation: Have you tried to FEEL the gum vending machine over there?
final English: Have you tried to FEEL the gum machine over there?

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんって　スプーンを　おれるように
なったって　ほんとうなの？
literal translation: Is it true that {NAME} became able to break spoons?
final English: {NAME}, is it true you can snap spoons in two now?

original Japanese:
すいぶん　ちょうしが　いいみたいね。
うらやましいわ！
literal translation: You seem to be in very good form. I envy you!
final English: You're doing so well lately. I'm so jealous!

original Japanese:
あそこにある　シンセサイザーを
フイール　してみた？
literal translation: Have you tried to FEEL the synthesizer over there?
final English: Have you tried to FEEL the synthesizer over there?

original Japanese:
もうすぐ　{NAME}さんも　サイマスターに
なれそうね！
literal translation: {NAME} also looks like they can become a Psi Master soon!
final English: You're almost ready to be a Psi Master, {NAME}!

original Japanese:
あなたの　バイブレーションで　くうかんが
ゆがみそうよ。　さすがね！
literal translation: Space looks like it will warp with your vibrations. As expected!
final English: Your vibrations could warp space itself. That's you, all right!

original Japanese:
サイランドで　ゲームを　やりすぎちゃったよ！
ちょうしに　のってると　サイパワーを　つかいすぎるから　{NAME}さんも　きをつけたほうがいいよ！
literal translation: I played too many games at Psi Land! If you get carried away you use too much Psi Power, so you'd better be careful too, {NAME}!
final English: I went overboard on the games at Psi Land! Get carried away and you'll use up too much Psi Power, so be careful, {NAME}!

original Japanese:
まだ　ゲームを　やってないのかい？
そうか………　{NAME}さんの　レベルでは
まだ　ゲームきを　コントロール　できないかもね。
literal translation: You haven't played the games yet? I see… At {NAME}'s level, maybe you can't control the game machines yet.
final English: You haven't tried the games yet? I see… At your level, {NAME}, you probably can't control the machines yet.

original Japanese:
サイランドで　れーすゲーム　を　やったかい？
ちょうのうりょくの　トレーニングにも　なるから
たまには　やってみるのも　いいんじゃないの。
literal translation: Have you played the race game at Psi Land? It's also psychic power training, so isn't it good to try it once in a while?
final English: Have you played the race game at Psi Land? It's good psychic training too, so why not give it a go now and then?

original Japanese:
いま　ひとりで　しずかに　のんでいるんだ………
わるいけど　じゃましないで　くれるかな。
literal translation: Right now I'm drinking quietly alone… Sorry, but could you not bother me?
final English: I'm having a quiet drink alone… Sorry, could you leave me be?

original Japanese:
サイランドで　かーどゲーム　を　やったかい？
あのゲームは　1と5を　いつだすかが　だいじなんだ！　ちゃんと　とうしすれば　かてるけどね。
literal translation: Have you played the card game at Psi Land? In that game, when you play the 1 and 5 is what matters! If you use Clairvoyance properly you can win, though.
final English: Have you played the card game at Psi Land? The key is when to play your 1 and 5! Use Clairvoyance right and you'll win.

original Japanese:
{NAME}さん　ちょうのうりょくを　つかうときは
せいこうした　ビジョン　だけを　おもいえがいたほうが　いいぞ！
literal translation: {NAME}, when using psychic power, you should picture only the vision of success!
final English: {NAME}, when you use ESP, picture nothing but a vision of success!

original Japanese:
サイランドで　ぱねるゲームを　やったかい？
ちゃんと　よち　を　つかわないと　かてないぞ！
literal translation: Have you played the panel game at Psi Land? You can't win unless you use Precognition properly!
final English: Have you played the panel game at Psi Land? You can't win unless you use Precognition properly!

original Japanese: いっしょに　のむ　かい？
literal translation: Will you drink with me?
final English: Care to join me for a drink?

original Japanese:
いまの　きぶんには　シンセサイザーの　おとが
あってるね。
literal translation: The sound of the synthesizer suits my current mood.
final English: That synthesizer sound really suits my mood right now.

original Japanese: さあ　また　ゲームを　プレイしに　いくとするか。
literal translation: Well, I guess I'll go play games again.
final English: Well, guess I'll go play some more games.

original Japanese: ずいぶん　エスパーらしい　バイブに　なってきたね
literal translation: Your vibes have become quite Esper-like.
final English: Your vibes are starting to feel like a real Esper's.

original Japanese:
いどうちゅうに　グルー　に　ためされて
しっぱいすると　おおきくポイントがさがるから
きをつけてね　ねんじれば　あいずらくなるわよ！
literal translation: If Guru tests you while traveling and you fail, your points drop a lot, so be careful. If you concentrate your will, he becomes harder to meet!
final English: If Guru tests you on the road and you fail, you lose lots of points. Watch out! Focus your will to run into him less often!

original Japanese:
レベルが　あがると
ポイントは　いちど　0　に
もどるのよ。
literal translation: When your level goes up, your points return to 0 once.
final English: When your level goes up, your points reset to 0.

original Japanese: がんばってね！
literal translation: Do your best!
final English: Good luck!

original Japanese: てんきが　いいから　きもちがいいね！
literal translation: The weather is nice, so it feels good!
final English: What lovely weather! It feels wonderful out!

original Japanese: その　ちょうしよ！
literal translation: That's the way!
final English: That's the spirit!

original Japanese: ずいぶん　ちょうしが　いいみたいね！
literal translation: You seem to be in very good form!
final English: You're really in the zone!

original Japanese: {NAME}さんが　ちょうのうりょくを　つかっているときって　とっても　いいかおを　しているわ！
literal translation: When {NAME} is using psychic power, you have a really good face!
final English: You get such a great look on your face when you use ESP, {NAME}!

original Japanese: ちょっと　つかれて　いるんじゃないの？
literal translation: Aren't you a little tired?
final English: Aren't you a little tired?

original Japanese: あまり　あせらないで　リラックスして　やってね！
literal translation: Don't be too impatient, relax and do it!
final English: Don't rush it. Just relax and take your time!

original Japanese:
わたしも　{NAME}さん　ぐらいの
バイブレーションに　はやく　なりたいな！
literal translation: I want to quickly reach vibrations like {NAME}'s too!
final English: I wish my vibrations were as strong as yours, {NAME}!

original Japanese: わたしも　サイマスター　に　なりたいわ！
literal translation: I want to become a Psi Master too!
final English: I want to be a Psi Master too!

original Japanese:
サイパワーを　つかうときは　1かいめで　せいこうさせるほうが　ポイントが　たかいよ。
5かい　いじょうは　トライできないんだ。
literal translation: When using Psi Power, succeeding on the first try gives higher points. You can't try 5 times or more.
final English: When you use Psi Power, you score more points if you succeed first try. You can't try more than five times.

original Japanese:
レベルが　あがると
サイイベントが　ふえるぞ！
literal translation: When your level goes up, Psi Events increase!
final English: Raise your level and you'll find more Psi Events!

original Japanese:
たまに　じぶんの　へやに　もどって　セーブ
したほうが　いいと　おもうよ。
literal translation: I think you should go back to your own room once in a while and save.
final English: I think you should head back to your room to save now and then.

original Japanese:
ねんりきで　ものを　しゅつげん　させることを
アポーツ　と　いうんだよね。
literal translation: Making an object appear with psychokinesis is called an 'apport,' isn't it.
final English: Making an object appear with Psychokinesis is called an "apport."

original Japanese:
たいようの　ひかり　を　あびながら
ちょうのうりょくの　トレーニングを　するのも
きもちが　いいよね。
literal translation: Doing psychic power training while bathing in the sunlight feels good too, doesn't it.
final English: Psychic training out in the sunshine feels great, doesn't it?

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんは　ねんしゃを　やったことある？
シャッターを　おさずに　ねんりきをつかって
フイルムを　かんこう　させてしまうことなのよ！
literal translation: {NAME}, have you ever done nensha? It's making film get exposed using psychokinesis without pressing the shutter!
final English: {NAME}, have you ever tried thoughtography? It's using Psychokinesis to expose film without pressing the shutter!

original Japanese:
うちゅう　から　ちきゅう　を　みたら
ちきゅう　も　ひとつの　ちいさな　ほしにしか
みえないだろうね。
literal translation: If you looked at the Earth from space, the Earth would probably look like nothing but one small star.
final English: Seen from space, I bet the Earth looks like just one tiny planet.

original Japanese:
サイパワーが　はたらいているときの　のうは　は
アルフアーは　じょうたいに　なっているんだってねのうはそくていき　で　しらべると　わかるよ。
literal translation: They say that when Psi Power is working, your brain waves are in an alpha-wave state. You can tell if you examine them with a brain-wave meter.
final English: They say Psi Power puts your brain waves in an alpha state.{P}You can see it on a brain-wave meter.

original Japanese:
レベルが　あがると
パワースポット　に　いけるそうだね。
ぼくも　まだ　いったことは　ないんだ。
literal translation: I hear when your level goes up you can go to the Power Spot. I haven't been there yet either.
final English: I hear you can go to the Power Spot once your level is high enough. I've never been there myself.

original Japanese:
パワースポットに　いくことが　できれば
さいごの　サイイベントに　ちょうせん　できる
らしいね。　でも　とても　むづかしいらしいよ。
literal translation: It seems if you can go to the Power Spot, you can challenge the final Psi Event. But it seems very difficult.
final English: They say if you can reach the Power Spot, you can take on the final Psi Event. But I hear it's really tough.

original Japanese: いつも　バイブレーションが　いいね！
literal translation: Your vibrations are always good!
final English: Your vibrations are always so good!

original Japanese:
このパークには　ひこうせんの　かくのうこが
あることを　{NAME}さんは　しってました？
literal translation: Did you know, {NAME}, that there's an airship hangar in this park?
final English: {NAME}, did you know there's a blimp hangar in this park?

original Japanese:
いちど　フイール　したばしょでも　もどってきたときや　レベルが　あがったときは　もういっかい
フイール　してみると　いいわよ。
literal translation: Even at places you've FELT once, when you come back or when your level goes up, it's good to try FEEL once more.
final English: Even if you've already used FEEL somewhere, try it again when you come back or after your level goes up!

original Japanese:
ちょうのうりよくで　はな　を　さかせることも
できるのよ。　{NAME}さんも　もうちょっと
レベルが　あがったら　やってみると　いいわ！
literal translation: You can also make flowers bloom with psychic power. {NAME}, once your level goes up a little more, you should try it!
final English: With psychic power, you can even make flowers bloom. Once your level's a bit higher, give it a try, {NAME}!

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんの　レベルなら　つぼみから　はなを
さかせることが　できそうよ。　パークの　はなを
さかせてみせてよ。　かだんを　フイール　してね！
literal translation: At {NAME}'s level, it seems you could make flowers bloom from buds. Show me by making the park's flowers bloom. FEEL the flower bed!
final English: At your level, {NAME}, you should be able to make buds bloom. Show me with the park's flowers. Just FEEL the flower bed!

original Japanese:
たまに　めいそう　を　するのも　ひつようじゃないかな？
バイブレーションが　あがるわよ！
literal translation: Isn't it necessary to meditate once in a while? Your vibrations will rise!
final English: Try meditating now and then. It'll raise your vibrations!

original Japanese:
そらに　うかんでいる　くもって　きれいよね。
くもを　みていると　ちきゅうの　バイブレーションを　かんじることが　できるわよ！
literal translation: The clouds floating in the sky are beautiful, aren't they. When you look at the clouds, you can feel the Earth's vibrations!
final English: Aren't the clouds floating in the sky lovely? Watching them, you can feel the Earth's vibrations!

original Japanese: サイパワー　の　つかいすぎに　ちゅういしてね！
literal translation: Be careful of using too much Psi Power!
final English: Be careful not to use too much Psi Power!

original Japanese:
ちょうのうりょくは　21せいきの　あたらしい
かがくと　なるに　ちがいないわ！
literal translation: Psychic power will surely become the new science of the 21st century!
final English: Psychic power is sure to be the new science of the 21st century!

original Japanese: いしきが　かくせい　してきたみたいね！
literal translation: It seems your consciousness has begun to awaken!
final English: Looks like your consciousness is awakening!

original Japanese: たまには　やすむことも　ひつようよ！
literal translation: Resting once in a while is necessary too!
final English: You need to rest once in a while!

original Japanese: もう　あなたは　さいこうの　レベルに　なったわ！
literal translation: You have now reached the highest level!
final English: You've reached the very highest level now!

original Japanese: なるほど…………
literal translation: I see…
final English: I see…

original Japanese: また　おあいしましょう。
literal translation: Let's meet again.
final English: Until we meet again.

original Japanese: それでは。
literal translation: Well then.
final English: Farewell, then.

original Japanese: ふーむ…………
literal translation: Hmm…
final English: Hmm…

original Japanese: バイブレーションが…………
literal translation: The vibrations…
final English: Those vibrations…

original Japanese: そうか…………
literal translation: I see… (so that's it)
final English: So that's how it is…

original Japanese:
{NAME}さんの　バイブレーションが
よく　わかりました。
literal translation: I understood {NAME}'s vibrations well.
final English: I have a good sense of your vibrations now, {NAME}.

original Japanese:
いまの　バイブレーションを　わすれないことだ！
つぎに　あうまでに　もっと　パワーバランスを
つけておくように。　わかったかな？
literal translation: Don't forget the vibrations you have now! By the time we next meet, build up more power balance. Do you understand?
final English: Don't forget the vibrations you have now! Work on your power balance before we meet again. Understood?

original Japanese:
ほう　なかなか　バイブレーションは　よかったぞ！だからといって　かしん　は　きんもつだ。
しょしんに　かえる。　これが　だいじだ！
literal translation: Oh, your vibrations were quite good! But that said, overconfidence is forbidden. Return to the beginner's mind. This is what matters!
final English: Oh-ho, impressive vibrations! But do not grow overconfident.{P}Keep a beginner's mind. That is what matters!

original Japanese:
よし　そのちょうしだ！
　む　の　きょうちに　なるまで　マインドパワーをきたえることが　だいじだ。
literal translation: Good, that's the way! Training your Mind Power until you reach the state of nothingness is what matters.
final English: Good, keep it up! What matters is training your Mind Power until you reach a state of no-mind.

original Japanese:
バイブレーションは　わるくは　なかったぞ！
しかし　わたしと　くらべると　まだまだ…………
literal translation: Your vibrations weren't bad! But compared to me, still not yet…
final English: Your vibrations were not bad! Still, next to mine, not even close…

original Japanese:
よし　なかなか　よかったぞ！
しかし　もうちょっと　よゆうが　あると
いいんだが…………
literal translation: Good, quite good! But if only you had a bit more composure…
final English: Good, quite good! But I'd like to see a little more composure…

original Japanese:
だいぶ　かんかくが　つかめた　ようだね。
このちょうしで　がんばるんだ！
literal translation: It seems you've gotten a good grasp of the feeling. Keep it up at this pace!
final English: Looks like you've really got the feel of it now. Keep it up!

original Japanese:
よーしよし！
いまの　かんかくを　わすれるな！
literal translation: Good, good! Don't forget the feeling you have now!
final English: Good, very good! Don't forget that feeling!

original Japanese:
そう　それだ！
あとは　コンスタントに　せいこう　させることだ。リラックスして　やることだね！
literal translation: Yes, that's it! The rest is to succeed constantly. Do it relaxed!
final English: Yes, that's it! Now do it consistently. Stay relaxed!

original Japanese:
うーん…………　どうしたんだい？
こんなことじゃ　エスパーとは　いえないぞ！
literal translation: Hmm… what's wrong? With this you can't be called an Esper!
final English: Hmm… what's wrong? You can't call yourself an Esper like this!

original Japanese:
なんだい　いまの　バイブレーションは？
ちっとも　かんじるものが　なかったぞ！
literal translation: What were those vibrations just now? I didn't feel anything at all!
final English: What were those vibrations? I didn't feel a thing!

original Japanese:
すこし　バイブレーションが　みだれていたぞ！
スクールで　めいそう　でも　やることだ。
literal translation: Your vibrations were a little disordered! Do something like meditation at the School.
final English: Your vibrations were scattered! Go meditate at the School.

original Japanese:
おや？　いまのは　なんだったのかな…………
そんなことでは　しろうと　と　いわれるぞ！
literal translation: Oh? What was that just now… With that, you'll be called an amateur!
final English: What was that just now… Keep that up and they'll call you an amateur!

original Japanese: あれ？　それで　サイパワーを　つかっているのかい{NAME}さんの　パワーは　あんてい　してないね！もっと　バランスよく　やらないと…………
literal translation: Huh? Is that you using Psi Power? {NAME}'s power isn't stable! If you don't do it with better balance…
final English: Call that Psi Power? You're unsteady, {NAME}! Work on your balance…

original Japanese:
こらこら！
てきとうに　やったら　だめだぞ！
しんけんに　やることが　だいじだ！
literal translation: Hey, hey! You mustn't do it carelessly! Doing it seriously is what matters!
final English: Now, now! Don't be careless! You must take this seriously!

original Japanese:
バイブレーションが　わるいぞ！
もういっかい　スクールに　にゅうがく　したほうがいいんじゃ　ないの？
literal translation: Your vibrations are bad! Wouldn't it be better to enroll in the School once more?
final English: Your vibrations are poor! Maybe re-enroll at the School?

original Japanese:
ほう　　たいしたもんだ！
よく　それで　スクールを　そつぎょう　できたね！
literal translation: Oh, quite something! You managed to graduate from the School with that!
final English: My, how impressive! You actually graduated from the School like that?

original Japanese:
まえのデータをけして
あらたにゲームをはじめますか？
literal translation: Erase the previous data and start a new game?
final English:
Erase old data
and start over?

うちゅう　は　バランス　のみだ。
そこに　ふかさとしての　リズム　がある。
literal translation: The universe is only balance. In it there is rhythm, as depth.
final English:
The universe is balance,
with rhythm as its depth.

くうかん　が　そくど　を　もつのであって
ひかり　が　そくど　を　もつのではない。

final English:
Space is what has speed.
Light itself has none.

ぶっしつ　は　ひかり　を　めざし
ひかり　は　ぶっしつ　を　うみつづける。
literal translation: Matter aims for light, and light goes on giving birth to matter.
final English:
Matter reaches for light.
Light creates matter anew.

original Japanese:
せいめい　も　うちゅう　も
ぜんたいとして　じぞくしている。
literal translation: Both life and the universe persist as a whole.
final English:
Life and the universe
endure as one whole.

original Japanese: そんざい　とは　ちょっかん　の　だいめいしである。
literal translation: Existence is a byword (pronoun) for intuition.
final English:
Existence is another
name for intuition.

original Japanese: げんご　は　はどう　の　ていちゃくである。
literal translation: Language is the fixing (settling) of waves/vibration.
final English:
Words are vibrations
that have settled.

original Japanese:
このソフトは　あなたの　せんざいいしきの
なかに　ねむっている　サイキックパワーを
ひきだすために　かいはつされた、
ちょうのうりょくかいはつソフトです。
エスパーキヨタの　たいけんに　もとづいて
げんみつに　シミュレートしているので
あなたの　マインドレベル　にあわせて
